steps.observed: 'What renders during the boot gap:' at line 232. Main lane renders LoadingState widget with spinner and 'Connecting to {api-base-url}...' text. Detail lane renders EmptyState with 'Select an agent to inspect'. Evidence lane collapsed. Status footer shows degraded indicator.

principlesNamed: Main Lane, Detail Lane, Evidence Lane

steps.observed: ## .gsx Toolchain section found starting around line ~377. Subtitled 'This section documents the .gsx code generation toolchain for LLM authors working on the TUI. It satisfies VAL-DOCS-010.'

Two exact commands provided: 'go generate github.com/grindlemire/go-tui/cmd/tui@v0.11.0 ./internal/interfaces/tui/...' and equivalently 'tui generate ./internal/interfaces/tui/...'. Both are concrete, not placeholders.

steps.action: Check (c): steps to add a new view without breaking generation
steps.observed: 'Add a New View' Checklist with 6 numbered steps: (1) Create .gsx source file, (2) Run regeneration command, (3) Write hand-written companion files, (4) Write tests, (5) Register new screen, (6) Commit both .gsx and *_gsx.go together.

steps.action: Check (d): list of generated artifact paths not to hand-edit
steps.observed: Generated Artifact Paths table: 'internal/interfaces/tui/shell_gsx.go' (from 'internal/interfaces/tui/shell.gsx'). Note also states: 'When new .gsx files are added, the corresponding *_gsx.go file joins this list.'

summary: Tested 5 assertions: all 5 passed. VAL-DOCS-003 (9 decisions with Decision/Rationale/Alternatives format and sub-requirements (c), (d), (f)): pass. VAL-DOCS-009 (Reconciliation section ≥150 words, both links, ≥3 DESIGN.md principles): pass — section has ~800+ words, both links present, 5 principles named. VAL-DOCS-010 (.gsx toolchain with concrete commands/globs/steps): pass — all 4 sub-requirements met with concrete values. VAL-DOCS-012 (traceability table ≥6 rows): pass — exactly 6 rows, each citing a decision with resolution. VAL-DOCS-014 (surface ownership with 5 DESIGN.md surfaces): pass — all 5 surfaces (Runtime, Companion, Rooms, Orchestration, Events) mapped with duplication resolutions.
